jd_requirements: Real-time software stack for industrial robots
Motion control algorithms, kinematics, trajectory planning
Perception, localization, mapping, path planning, sensor fusion
Hardware-software integration across mechanical, electrical, controls teams
Sensors, actuators, PLCs, industrial controllers synchronization
System calibration, network synchronization, timing optimization
Reusable drivers, middleware layers, communication interfaces
Simulation environments, HIL testing, real-time telemetry
Metrics, logging, data analytics for system performance
Deployment and lifecycle support in production environments

bullets.text: Developed control programs for a six-axis CRP2 robotic arm using embedded C and ladder logic, enabling automated multi-axis motion for fuel rod testing.
Designed an STM32F103-based gateway to enable Modbus RTU communication between the PC and robotic controller, ensuring stable and real-time data exchange.

bullets.text: Led a 5-member cross-functional team to develop a hybrid flying-driving robot platform, achieving 100% integration of mobility and flight subsystems.
Developed a ROS2-based robotic system integrating a simulator and MPC controller, enabling precise obstacle avoidance and full trajectory completion with real-time state logging.
Integrated OptiTrack motion capture system with the robotic platform, achieving <1 mm position accuracy and <10 ms latency, supporting real-time position feedback for closed-loop control.

edits.before: Integrated OptiTrack motion capture system with robotic platform, achieving <1 mm position accuracy and <10 ms latency, supporting real-time position feedback for closed-loop control in indoor environments.
edits.after: Integrated OptiTrack motion capture system with the robotic platform, achieving <1 mm position accuracy and <10 ms latency, supporting real-time position feedback for closed-loop control.
edits.reason: Removed 'in indoor environments' for brevity; added 'the' for grammar; no factual change.

bullets.text: Applied control system design and experimental validation to establish an OptiTrack-based real-time feedback pose control system, enabling sub-centimeter trajectory tracking and iterative controller refinement.

Managed three interdisciplinary teams over a six-month project, overseeing a $20,000 budget; delivered two autonomous ring-handling systems and one joystick-controlled quadruped within all milestones.
Developed embedded C firmware for STM32F407, enabling CAN-based motor control, BLE remote communication, and PID position control with +/-2 mm tracking error for an omnidirectional mobile robot.
Designed a modular PID-based navigation system on STM32 with inverse kinematics and yaw compensation, achieving omnidirectional motion and +/-0.1% global localization accuracy.
Implemented a custom UART protocol with headers, footers, and float unpacking; used DMA + interrupts for non-blocking 100 Hz updates of 6-DoF data, with <0.2% error rate.

Modularized the robot into gimbal, power, launcher, and chassis to achieve independent functionality and decoupled operation, incorporating modular interfaces and redundancy to improve system stability and debuggability.

Designed a compact, low-power crane system with ESP32-based Wi-Fi remote control, enabling low-latency communication and autonomous coordination across multiple devices, achieving over 95% task repeatability.
Independently developed an STM32-based control system using fuzzy PID algorithms for closed-loop stepper motor control, achieving +/-1 mm positioning accuracy.

Consolidated five functional boards into a single 4-layer PCB with KiCad, integrating control, power, and communication modules; reduced overall footprint by 40% and verified signal integrity via 100-MHz oscilloscope.
Collaborated with industry engineers to migrate fuzzy PID logic and the remote control interface to a PLC platform, enabling compatibility with standard industrial automation workflows.
